name: Low Earth Orbit
story: The closest band of space — 160 to 2,000 km up. Short comms latency (~7 ms one-way), atmospheric drag still tugs at the lower edge, and the radiation belts haven't kicked in yet. Crewed spaceflight lives here for the same reasons: rescuable, reachable, and the human body tolerates a few-hundred-kilometre commute. Every space station that has ever flown has parked in LEO.
comparison: About 1/600th of the way to the Moon. The ISS at 408 km orbits at the same altitude as the distance from London to Geneva — laid sideways.
